Members of the public wishing to make public comment may do so in one of the following

(1) By directly addressing the Planning Commission in person at the time(s) allotted on the agenda

out a speaker card providing their name and indicating whether they wish to address the Planning
Commission on an item(s) of business appearing under (i) the Public Hearing portion of the agenda;

13.  Commissioner’s Comments
Commissioner Salas had a question about the residential property that burned down twice at
Peck and Ranchito 6-8 months ago. He wanted to know if there was a plan to remove the debris.
City Planner Elias said that because there is a Code Enforcement case open on this property
that owners are allowed a certain amount of time to address the debris. Both he and
Commissioner Quiñones expressed thanks to city staff for their diligence in the approval
process.

Commissioner Tamashiro followed up with a question on bus stop signage that had been
brought up in the last meeting. CED Director Fowler stated that Public Works was informed and
that they had already spoken to the bus companies who were investigating the issue.

Commissioner Tamashiro asked city staff how El Monte is addressing the issue of businesses
closing down around the city; he brought up that other cities have incentives for businesses.
CED Director Fowler shared that a small business grant has been available for El Monte
businesses. Commissioner Quiñones asked if a meeting could be setup for business owners to
promote the grant. CED Director Fowler stated that the grant has been promoted on social
media, via the city website, and applications have been hand delivered to various businesses,
including those that have open Code Enforcement cases.

PROJECT/APPLICANT INFORMATION:

Subject Property:  10561 Santa Fe Drive (APN: 8578-022-002)
Project Applicant:  Miguel Vasquez
Property Owner:  TPMC Services, LLC

BACKGROUND:

On August 30, 2022, the City of El Monte Planning Commission adopted Resolution 3641
(Attachment A) approving Design Review (DR) No. 12-22 to construct a five-story, 212-
unit apartment complex at the subject site mentioned above. The entitlement approval
became effective on September 9, 2022 with an expiration date of September 9, 2023.

On June 30, 2023, the Planning Division received a request for a 12-month time extension
for DR 12-22. Additional time was needed to transfer the property ownership and secure
construction permits. A time extension was granted with an expiration date of September
9, 2024.

On June 26, 2024, the Planning Division received a request for a 12-month time extension
for DR 12-22. In reviewing the request, it was determined that Ordinance No. 3023,
adopted May 2, 2023, allows Design Reviews to be valid for two (2) years after the effective
date of approval (EMMC Section 17.122.050(A)). As such it was determined that the
Community & Economic Development Director was able to administratively approve of the

  TIME EXTENSION (EXT) NO. 36-2026 | 10561 SANTA FE DRIVE | 1
 time extension request with an expiration date of September 9, 2025. The applicant may
request an additional extension, which shall be considered by the Planning Commission.

On July 14, 2025, the Planning Division received a request for a 12-month time extension
for DR 12-22. Additional time was requested to update the plans with the required
California Building Code requirements and secure construction funding in order to obtain
permits and commence construction. A time extension was granted with an expiration
date of September 9, 2026.

REQUEST:

On August 17, 2026, prior to the expiration of entitlements, the Planning Division received
a request for a 12-month time extension for DR 12-22. Additional time is requested to
finalize negotiations and enter into an agreement for the joint venture to develop the
project.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission extend the project’s entitlement for an
additional one (1) year with a new expiration date of September 9, 2027.

 HOUSING ELEMENT IMPLEMENTATION:

On February 1, 2022, the City Council approved the 2021-2029 General Plan Housing
Element Update. Staff subsequently submitted the Housing Element to the California
Department of Housing and Community Development (“HCD”). Program No. 1 of the
implementation plan calls for the following items to be incorporated as part of the
Comprehensive Zoning Code updates:
  • Develop an Urban Housing Zone along the Garvey Avenue Corridor and 5- Points
  Area;
  • Allow residential densities of up to 50 units per acre and building heights of up to 5
  or 6 stories;
  • Allow multiple-family residential projects to be approved by right (i.e., without a
  Conditional Use Permit);
  • Establish minimum densities for residential-only projects and mixed-use projects
  that include housing; and
  • Reduce parking and open space requirements and increase the allotted floor area
  for higher density residential projects.

The City Council adopted Ordinance No. 3023 on May 2, 2023 to implement Program 5,
and Ordinance No. 3053 implementing Program 1 on May 14, 2025.

After the California Court of Appeal, Second Appellate District published New Commune
DTLA LLC v. City of Redondo Beach (2025) 115 Cal.App.5th 111, HCD sent the City a
Letter of Technical Assistance stating that, upon review of Ordinance Nos. 3023 and 3053,
the City must undertake further rezoning to implement Programs 1 and 5 and satisfy all
requirements in Government Code section 65583.2, subdivisions (h) and (i). Specifically,
HCD requested that:

  •  Mixed-use sites must permit one hundred percent (100%) residential
  development and must require that a minimum of fifty percent (50%) of
  the total square footage be dedicated to residential uses.
  •  Sites must permit owner-occupied and rental multifamily uses by right
  for developments in which twenty percent (20%) or more of the units
  are set for affordable or lower income housing.
  •  Sites identified for lower income housing in the Housing Element must
  allow a minimum density of twenty (20) dwelling units per acre (“du/ac”).

Staff developed the proposed amendments in consultation with HCD to address the above
requirements.

  land uses and provision of utilities) for the requested/anticipated land
  uses/developments.

  3
   Finding of Fact:

  AMEND NO. 4-2026 would allow for the advancement of the implementation of
  Program No. 1 of the 2021-2029 General Plan Housing Element, which allows for
  uses that are physically suitable and compatible.

C. The Amendments are consistent with the purpose, goals and policies of the City’s
  General Plan.

  Finding of Fact:

  AMEND NO. 4-2026 implements a significant number of General Plan goals and
  policies. These are primarily found in the Land Use Element and Housing Element
  and includes the following:

  Land Use Element
  Goal LU-2 – Revitalization and redevelopment of residential, commercial and
  industrial areas through the sensitive integration of infill development, elimination
  of blight, and master planning efforts:

  • LU-2.1 – Underutilized Uses. Facilitate and increase the concentration of
  commercial and industrial uses to activity centers, major intersections and
  other focused areas;
  • LU-2.2 – Midblock Residential. Introduce midblock residential uses, such as
  mixed/multiuse housing, condominiums, apartments and live-work units to
  stimulate the revitalization and reuse of major corridors and removal of
  underused and incompatible uses; and
  • LU-2.4 – Planning Tools. Utilize specific plans, planned developments and
  specialized zoning districts to foster cohesive and well-designed residential,
  mixed-use, commercial, and industrial districts. This can be applied to large
  vacant lands or for the reuse of existing properties or for a district/ subdistrict.

  Land Use Element

  GOAL LU-9 – Recreate vibrant commercial corridors with the introduction of a mix
  of higher density residential uses, sensitively integrated commercial uses
  concentrated at critical nodes and tree-lined streetscapes that are aesthetically
  pleasing, encourage walking, and inspire community pride:

  • LU-9.1 – Corridor Reuse. Promote the reuse of strip commercial and
  industrial corridors by consolidating retail and commercial uses into activity
  nodes and transitioning intervening areas for midblock residential or
  mixed/multiuse developments;
  • LU-9.2 – Housing Types. Sensitively integrate higher density residential
  uses (e.g., townhomes, stacked units, live-work, etc.) along Peck Road and

  4
   Durfee Avenue. Incorporate urban density residential uses along Garvey
  Avenue and at Five Points;
  • LU-9.3 – Prohibited Uses. Prohibit industrial and commercial uses along
  major corridors that detract from residential neighborhoods and adjacent
  residential uses; and
  • LU-9.8 – Lot Consolidation. Develop a sliding scale of residential densities –
  i.e. the larger the property or the greater the number of merged parcels, the
  greater the residential density, as permitted per the Land Use Plan for
  mixed/multiuse and urban/multiuse housing.

2021-2029 Housing Element

Goal H-2 – Adequate sites for new housing that create a vibrant downtown,
revitalize transportation corridors with quality housing, and motivate reinvestment
and revitalization in neighborhoods.

  • H-2.1 – Housing Sites. Provide adequate sites through land use, zoning, and
  specific plan designations to allow single-family homes, multi-family homes,
  Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs), urban housing, mixed-use housing,
  mobile homes and special needs housing.
  • H-2.4 – Urban Housing. Provide zoning designations necessary to develop
  urban housing at high densities along Garvey Avenue Corridor and the 5-
  Points Area, providing for linkages to transit, commercial activity and
  communities like parks and recreation centers.
  • H-2.5 – Major Corridors. Direct the production of quality mixed/multiuse
  projects along major corridors Durfee Avenue, Peck Road, and Garvey
  Avenue to allow for efficient land use practices, improved mobility and
  energy conservation.
  • H-2.6 – Work/Live and Live/Work. Provide opportunities for work/live and
  live/work housing in the Downtown Core, along major corridors and within
  the Flair Business Park.
  • H-2.9 – Neighborhood Protection. Protect established single-family
  neighborhoods, through measures including use of zoning standards and
  objective design standards, from the transition, intensification and
  encroachment of nonresidential uses and higher density housing that
  detracts from the character of the neighborhood.
  • H-2.10 – Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Housing. Support the
  development of TODs, which contain a variety of mixed-use projects
  vertically or horizontally integrated with commercial, professional,
  entertainment and recreational uses.

Goal H-3 – A diversity of quality housing types and prices that meet the needs of
residents, support the economic development and revitalization, and provide
opportunities for residents of all ages and income levels:

  5
   • H-3.7 – Diverse Housing. Support the production of varied housing types,
  including single-family, townhomes, apartments and special needs housing
  that are priced at levels affordable to all income levels.
